judgements.justification: Both committees found the writing mostly clear and shared the same clarity gaps; the split rested on novelty and evaluation, not on clarity.
No score moved after the rebuttal in either committee.
B's AC counted all four below-threshold ratings, and A had no detractor to set aside.
No A reviewer rated above 7, and A's praise took the paper's framing at face value rather than resting on a checked reading.
No reviewer in either committee admitted reading only part of the paper.
B doubted the value of VQG as a task, which R18 covers; no reviewer read the paper from a rival theoretical tradition.
A's meta-review argued only that the paper is 'clearly above the bar of NeurIPS' and gave no reason for a spotlight over ratings 7, 6, 7, 7.
B's reviewers knew DH-VQG [19] and checked the margins and missing baselines against it, while A's reviewers called the evaluation comprehensive and the double-hint problem 'new'.
B's AC correctly wrote that all reviewers recommend reject; no meta-review misstated final positions toward a lower decision.
B's AC suggested a vision or NLP venue only in passing; B rejected for limited novelty and unshown benefit, not for a narrow audience of a sound paper.
Neither committee had a low-scoring reviewer whose misreading forced the AC to argue only for acceptance.
Both committees received the same zero-shot table; no new results went to one committee only.
No committee had a lone high-confidence expert rating above lower-confidence reviewers; confidences were 4 to 5 in A and all 4 in B.
Reviewer_tJc4's 2021-09-01 note restated earlier concerns and changed no score; no new objection entered after the response period.
A's review texts were positive and B's negative, so the rating gap matches the verbal assessments.
B noted DH-GAN is close to DH-VQG, but rejected on novelty and missing evidence, not on an overstated headline claim capping the tier.
A's reviewers rated 7, 6, 7, 7 at confidence 4 to 5, not flat marginal-accept scores at low confidence.
